newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Richter gives forecast for Curiosin sales. [CORRECTED 19:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Richter gives forecast for Curiosin sales. [CORRECTED 19:45 GMT]

text.p: Hungarian pharmaceutical company Richter Gedeon Rt said on Wednesday it expected to sell 10,000 to 15,000 units of Curiosin, a new drug for treating ulcers and other sores, in Hungary in the fourth quarter.

"Richter believes this product will be a success on the market and it will be profitable but I can't disclose information about the amount (of profit)," Istvan Greiner, head of Richter's research and development department, told a news conference.

Curiosin is the result of Richter's own research and development. Richter planned to increase its total research and development spending to 2.3 billion forints in 1996 from 1.7 billion forints in 1995 (corrects from "The company expects to spend 2.3 billion forints on the product this year, up from 1.7 billion in 1995").
The liquid medicine is aimed at treating leg ulcers, bed sores and wounds that usually heal slowly.

"According to statistical data one to 1.5 percent of the population suffers from these illnesses, which means an additional 25 percent in costs in addition to the costs of the basic illness," Richter said in a statement.
Richter has applied for approval to sell the drug in a number of neighbouring countries, Beata Furka, head of market intelligence, said.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange Richter shares closed at 8,450 forints, up 200.
